extracted.intended_audience: inventors, companies, and patent attorneys preparing or amending European patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and EPO requirements for filing colour or greyscale patent drawings in European patent applications (including handling for Euro‑PCT filings and amendments). Advises on technical specs, strategic use of colour, and interactions with other patent offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability date and filing mode
rubrics_metrics.description: The new regulation comes into force on October 1, 2025. All European patent applications filed electronically on or after that date may include colour or greyscale drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colour/greyscale acceptance applies to electronically filed European applications filed on or after Oct 1, 2025; amendments including colour may also be filed from that date for existing applications (subject to added‑matter rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted drawing types
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO will officially accept colour and greyscale drawings in electronically filed applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces the prior practice where colour submissions were converted to black and white at publication, which could cause loss of information; use of colour enables a more faithful representation of inventions where colour is meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical image quality requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Colour drawings for patents must have well-defined lines, high contrast, and be perfectly visible at a 300 dpi resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure images are clear and unambiguous so the representation corresponds exactly to what is intended to be protected; meet resolution and contrast standards to avoid interpretation issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euro‑PCT handling and PATENTSCOPE requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: International (PCT) publication currently remains in black and white; for the EPO to accept colour drawings in the European phase of a Euro‑PCT application, the drawings must be available in colour on the PATENTSCOPE database and the international publication must mention this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a crucial technical detail: failure to have the colour version available and referenced in the international publication can lead the EPO to consider the colour version not part of the original application, affecting the scope of protection. Plan this step carefully when using PCT routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and added‑matter prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments including colour drawings may be filed for existing applications from Oct 1, 2025, but these new drawings must not add subject‑matter that extends beyond the original disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding colour must not broaden the technical content beyond the original filing; improper amendments risk affecting the patent’s validity. Coordinate with counsel when submitting amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use colour only when it adds descriptive value
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to use colour only when it provides real, clarifying value for describing the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If black and white is sufficient for a complete understanding, it remains the safest and most universal option—particularly if seeking protection in countries that do not yet accept colour. Consider whether colour materially improves disclosure before including it.

rubrics_metrics.name: International office differences and prosecution strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Different patent offices treat colour drawings differently: some already accept colour (e.g., KIPO; USPTO and CNIPA accept when necessary) while others (e.g., JPO and UKIPO) currently require black and white.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When pursuing protection in multiple jurisdictions, prepare high‑quality black and white drawings that meet all offices’ requirements as a baseline; if colour is indispensable, plan the strategy with a patent attorney to manage office‑specific rules and conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for colour drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The European Patent Office has not announced any additional official fees for filing colour drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing costs remain the same according to current announcements, though practitioners should monitor for future fee changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural risk when using colour in international filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The main risk is procedural: an international (PCT) publication in black and white can prevent the EPO from recognising a colour version in the European phase unless the colour version is properly available and referenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the inclusion of colour in PCT/EPO prosecution as a technical procedural step requiring careful handling by experienced counsel to avoid unintentional loss or narrowing of rights.
